python_modules.docstring:
Bounded, disk-backed staging, NOT an alternative TACTIC asset repository.

Chunks are fsynced before acknowledging their offset. Advisory file locks work
across processes on a LOCAL filesystem. NFS/SMB lock/durability semantics are not
claimed. A crash at the DB/filesystem boundary is explicitly 'uncertain'; it is
never retried automatically. Tickets/passwords and arbitrary client paths are
never persisted. Only the final callback may perform the original check-in.

python_modules.docstring:
Run the ORIGINAL TACTIC CherryPy server, with a private project-local runtime.
No test backend is imported. Existing config is never upgraded or overwritten.
Fresh SQLite initialization is explicit, uses the shipped TACTIC seed and its
original upgrade commands, and fails closed if any upgrade step reports errors.

Cooperative local server/upgrade lock, with shared cluster lifetime ownership.

Standalone/upgrade use exclusive mode. The cluster supervisor and every worker
hold shared mode, so an orphaned worker still prevents an offline upgrade.
A second, exclusive owner lock prevents two supervisors starting one install.
Old local launchers' exclusive flock/msvcrt locks conflict with this byte range.

Stage/validate/publish a managed LOCAL SQLite upgrade; no in-place retry.

Only installations created by INIT_LOCAL_SQLITE are accepted. The original
upgrade worker runs against copies. Existing configs, assets and templates are
not replaced. A durable promotion journal and retained original files protect
multi-database publication; a pending journal blocks normal startup.
